stories.headline: EU Approves €90B Loan for Ukraine and 20th Sanctions Package After Hungary Lifts Veto

key_facts.fact: The EU approved a €90 billion ($106 billion) loan package for Ukraine to cover economic and military needs for the next two years, after Hungary lifted its veto.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine desperately needs the 90-billion-euro ($106 billion) loan package to prop up its war-ravaged economy and help keep Russian forces at bay. Hungary angered its EU partners by reneging on a December deal to provide the funds.

key_facts.fact: Russian oil resumed flowing through the Druzhba pipeline to Slovakia after a three-month halt, removing the key obstacle to Hungary and Slovakia lifting their veto.
key_facts.excerpt: The flow resumed after three months at 2 a.m. Thursday, the Slovak economy ministry said, lifting a major obstacle to approving the EU funds for Ukraine later Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The 20th sanctions package targets Russian energy revenues, shadow fleet, crypto, and military-industrial complex, banning transactions with 20 Russian banks and imposing a sectoral ban on Russian crypto providers.
key_facts.excerpt: Transaction ban on 20 Russian banks. Sectoral ban on Russian crypto providers/platforms. Ban on transactions in RUBx (Russian crypto) and EU operators access for the digital rouble.

key_facts.fact: 46 additional vessels were banned (total: 632), and the EU activated its anti-circumvention tool for the first time, restricting exports to Kyrgyzstan over re-exports of sanctioned goods to Russia.
key_facts.excerpt: 46 additional vessels banned (total: 632), targeting shadow fleet tankers. Ban for EU operators to export CNC machines and certain radios to Kyrgyzstan (high re-export risk to Russia).

key_facts.fact: The sanctions include expanded export bans worth €360M+ and import bans worth €570M+, covering lab glassware, lubricants, chemicals, metals, and minerals.
key_facts.excerpt: Expanded export bans (€360M+ value): Laboratory glassware, high-performance lubricants, energetic materials, chemicals. Expanded import bans (€570M+ value): Raw materials, metals, minerals, steel scraps.

key_facts.fact: 16 entities in third countries (China, UAE, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Belarus) face sanctions for supplying dual-use goods or weapons to Russia.
key_facts.excerpt: Including 16 entities in third countries (China, UAE, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Belarus) supplying dual-use goods/weapons to Russia.

sources.outlet: AP via Chattanooga Times Free Press

stories.headline: Meta Cuts 8,000 Jobs and Closes 6,000 Roles as AI Capital Spending Hits $135B

key_facts.fact: Meta will lay off approximately 8,000 employees (10% of workforce) on May 20 and close 6,000 open roles, bringing the effective headcount reduction to 14,000 positions.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta is cutting approximately 8,000 employees (10% of its workforce) beginning 20 May, cancelling 6,000 open roles, and planning additional cuts for H2 2026.

key_facts.fact: The layoffs were announced in an internal memo by CPO Janelle Gale, who said they are part of 'our continued effort to run the company more efficiently and to allow us to offset the other investments we're making.'
key_facts.excerpt: We're doing this as part of our continued effort to run the company more efficiently and to allow us to offset the other investments we're making.

key_facts.fact: Meta's guided capital expenditure for 2026 is $115B to $135B, a 73% increase over the $72.2B spent in 2025, largely directed at AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's capital expenditure for 2026 is a 73% increase over the $72.2 billion it spent in 2025, largely directed at AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Additional job cuts are planned for H2 2026; if the second wave matches the first, Meta will have eliminated roughly 20% of its pre-2026 workforce.
key_facts.excerpt: Further layoffs are being planned 'in the second half of the year,' with the numbers still to be determined based on how well AI systems in the company are able to create efficiencies.

key_facts.fact: Meta also told employees earlier this week that a new tracking tool will capture keystrokes and mouse movements from work computers to train AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta employees received a memo stating that the company is installing new software on their computers that will track click locations, keystrokes, and mouse movements in an effort to train AI models.

key_facts.fact: CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on Meta's January earnings call that 2026 would be 'the year that AI starts to dramatically change the way that we work.'
key_facts.excerpt: On Meta's January earnings call, he called 2026 'the year that AI starts to dramatically change the way that we work.'

stories.headline: US Accuses China of Industrial-Scale AI Distillation; Beijing Orders Tech Firms to Reject US Capital

key_facts.fact: White House OSTP Director Michael Kratsios wrote in a memo that the US has intelligence indicating 'foreign entities, principally based in China' are conducting 'industrial-scale distillation' of American AI models using tens of thousands of surrogate accounts.
key_facts.excerpt: Foreign entities primarily based in China have conducted 'industrial-scale' campaigns to crib frontier AI models from US companies, Michael Kratsios, White House director of the office of science and technology policy, said in a memo.

key_facts.fact: The White House plans to share intelligence with US AI companies, coordinate private-sector defenses, develop best practices, and explore measures to hold foreign actors accountable for distillation campaigns.
key_facts.excerpt: The administration said it would work with US AI firms to counter such campaigns; the companies themselves recently banded together to share information about so-called adversarial distillation attempts.

key_facts.fact: In a parallel move, Chinese regulators including the NDRC told tech firms such as ByteDance, Moonshot AI, and StepFun to reject US capital without state approval, responding to Meta's acquisition of Chinese AI startup Manus.
key_facts.excerpt: China plans to restrict its leading technology companies, including top AI startups, from accepting US capital without first obtaining government approval... The move was reportedly in response to Meta's controversial acquisition of startup Manus.

key_facts.fact: The House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced bipartisan export control bills on April 22 that would close loopholes allowing China to access US AI technology, including considering listing distillation entities on the Entity List.
key_facts.excerpt: The House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced a slate of bipartisan export control bills Wednesday that show a growing appetite in Congress for restricting the flow of artificial intelligence technology to China.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has previously accused DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax of conducting distillation attacks against Claude; OpenAI has made similar accusations against DeepSeek for using GPT outputs to train its models.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this year, Anthropic described distillation 'attacks' by three AI laboratories, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax, saying it had found them all to be working to copy Anthropic models through distillation campaigns.

key_facts.fact: The dual escalation came weeks before a planned Trump visit to Beijing, with China's embassy responding that its AI development 'is the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation.'
key_facts.excerpt: A representative of China's US embassy in Washington DC said its development was 'the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation'.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Regeneron's Otarmeni, First Gene Therapy for Genetic Hearing Loss, Free in the US

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha), the first gene therapy for genetic hearing loss and the first FDA-approved gene therapy to restore a neurosensory function to normal levels.
key_facts.excerpt: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. has received accelerated approval for OtarmeniTM, the first gene therapy and second new molecular entity approved under the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program.

key_facts.fact: In the CHORD trial, 80% of the 20 evaluable pediatric patients achieved or surpassed the primary hearing endpoint at week 24, and with longer follow-up, 42% achieved normal hearing.
key_facts.excerpt: Pivotal results of the CHORD trial demonstrating 80% of participants achieved or surpassed a hearing level meeting the primary endpoint, and with longer follow-up, 42% achieved normal hearing.

key_facts.fact: Regeneron will make Otarmeni available for free in the United States and announced a drug pricing deal with the White House.
key_facts.excerpt: Regeneron said the therapy Otarmeni will be available for free to patients in the United States. Regeneron is also set to announce a drug pricing deal with the White House this afternoon.

key_facts.fact: OTOF-related hearing loss is ultra-rare, affecting 20-50 newborns per year in the US. Otarmeni delivers a functioning OTOF gene to inner ear hair cells via an infusion into the cochlea under general anesthesia.
key_facts.excerpt: OTOF hearing loss is ultra-rare, diagnosed in about 50 newborns per year in the U.S., according to Regeneron.

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Otarmeni just 61 days after Regeneron submitted its biologics license application, making it the sixth approval under the National Priority Voucher program and the first for a gene therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA said it approved Otarmeni 61 days after Regeneron submitted its biologics license application. It's the sixth approval under this program and the first for a gene therapy.

key_facts.fact: Regeneron acquired Decibel Therapeutics, which originally developed the therapy (then called DB-OTO), in 2023 for up to $213 million including milestones.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2023, Regeneron acquired Decibel in a deal set to pay out $213 million including milestone payments.

stories.headline: Cohere and Aleph Alpha Merge Into $20B Transatlantic AI Company for Sovereign AI

key_facts.fact: Canada's Cohere and Germany's Aleph Alpha agreed to merge into a combined entity valued at approximately $20 billion, intended as an alternative to US AI providers for governments and enterprises.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere and Aleph Alpha have agreed to merge, creating what Handelsblatt described as a combined entity valued at approximately $20 billion.

key_facts.fact: Cohere shareholders will receive approximately 90% of the combined entity and Aleph Alpha shareholders ~10%, making it effectively a Cohere acquisition. CEO Aidan Gomez will lead the combined company.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere's shareholders are set to receive approximately 90% of the combined company; Aleph Alpha's shareholders approximately 10%.

key_facts.fact: The combined company will have its global headquarters in Toronto and its European headquarters in Berlin. Germany's Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger and Canada's Evan Solomon attended the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The combined entity will have its global headquarters in Toronto and its European headquarters in Berlin. The deal is supported by the Canadian and German governments.

key_facts.fact: Aleph Alpha backer Schwarz Group will invest $600 million in Cohere's upcoming Series E funding round.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere also announced that the Schwarz Group, a German conglomerate, will invest US$600-million in financing for an upcoming funding round.

key_facts.fact: The German government is set to become an anchor customer of the merged entity as part of a broader European push for digital sovereignty and reduced dependence on US tech giants.
key_facts.excerpt: The German government is set to become an anchor customer. The move is seen as a political move by both Canada and Germany to counterbalance their dependence on American AI.

stories.headline: DOJ Arrests US Soldier for $400K+ Polymarket Insider Bet on Maduro Capture He Helped Plan

key_facts.fact: Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a 38-year-old Army special forces soldier at Fort Bragg, was charged with wire fraud, commodities fraud, and theft of nonpublic government information — the first criminal case in the US tied to prediction market wagers.
key_facts.excerpt: The Justice Department and CFTC unsealed an indictment charging Van Dyke with wire fraud, commodities fraud, theft of nonpublic government information — marking the first criminal case in the U.S. tied to prediction market wagers.

key_facts.fact: Van Dyke participated in the planning and execution of the January 2026 predawn raid that captured Maduro, then bet approximately $33,034 across 13 wagers on Polymarket that Maduro would be removed from power, earning over $409,000 in profits.
key_facts.excerpt: The soldier, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, 'participated in the planning and execution of the' operation to capture Maduro, the DOJ said.

key_facts.fact: The CFTC separately filed a civil complaint seeking restitution, disgorgement, trading bans, and a permanent injunction against further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act.
key_facts.excerpt: The CFTC is also pursuing civil penalties, seeking restitution, disgorgement, trading bans, and a permanent injunction against further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act.

key_facts.fact: Van Dyke faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted of the top count (wire fraud) and up to 10 years on each remaining count.
key_facts.excerpt: He faces a maximum possible sentence of 20 years in prison if convicted of the top criminal count, wire fraud, and up to 10 years in each of the remaining counts.

key_facts.fact: Trump, when asked about the arrest, said: 'The whole world, unfortunately, has become somewhat of a casino.' Trump's son Donald Jr. is both an investor in Polymarket and a paid adviser to rival Kalshi.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump, when asked about Van Dyke's arrest and other cases of suspected insider trading on prediction markets, said, 'You know the whole world, unfortunately, has become somewhat of a casino.'

key_facts.fact: Israeli authorities in February arrested several people and charged two on suspicion of using classified information to place bets about military operations in Iran on Polymarket.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli authorities in February arrested several people and charged two on suspicion of using classified information to place bets about military operations in Iran on Polymarket.

stories.headline: Trump Threatens 'Big Tariff' on UK If It Doesn't Drop Its 2% Digital Services Tax

key_facts.fact: Trump told reporters at the White House that the US will 'put a big tariff on the UK' if Britain does not drop its digital services tax, which he views as unfairly targeting American tech companies like Apple, Google, and Meta.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States will retaliate with a 'big tariff' if Britain continues to target companies like Apple, Alphabet's Google and Meta with its technology tax.

key_facts.fact: The UK's 2% digital services tax, introduced in 2020, generated £944 million in the 2025-26 fiscal year (up 17% YoY) and is projected to raise £1.4 billion annually by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Recent data from HM Revenue and Customs showed that the DST generated £944 million in the 2025–26 fiscal year, up 17% from the previous year. Official projections suggest the tax could raise £1.4 billion annually by 2030.

key_facts.fact: The warning comes ahead of King Charles III's state visit to the US next week; Trump said the monarch could help repair Washington's relationship with Britain, which has become strained.
key_facts.excerpt: His comments come ahead of a visit by Britain's head of state, King Charles, next week. Trump said he believes the monarch could help repair the Washington's relationship with the British.

key_facts.fact: Trump said: 'I don't like it when they target American companies, because basically, you're talking about our great American companies... We've been looking at it, and we can meet that very easily by just putting a big tariff on the UK.'
key_facts.excerpt: I don't like it when they target American companies, because basically, you're talking about our great American companies, whether we like those companies that don't like them, they're American companies and the top companies in the world.

key_facts.fact: The DST has been criticized by both Trump and his predecessor Joe Biden. The UK has so far resisted Washington's calls to drop the tax, maintaining it ensures digital businesses contribute fairly based on their economic activity in the country.
key_facts.excerpt: The United Kingdom rolled out its 2% digital services tax in 2020, a move that has been criticized by Trump and his predecessor Democrat Joe Biden.
